## Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi Endorses Connie Chan for Congress
“I am honored to receive Speaker Emerita Pelosi's endorsement and I am grateful and humbled by the support I've received from thousands of San Franciscans who have joined this campaign. Speaker Emerita Pelosi has shown by example what we can do when we stand together and we will now fight to make sure our beloved city remains a place of opportunity for all San Franciscans, and the conscience of our nation.”

***PRESS RELEASE***

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Contact: press@conniechansf.com
March 16, 2026

   Connie Chan Earns Sole Endorsement of the California Federation of Labor Unions
         Latest Endorsement Confirms Chan is THE Candidate for Working People

SAN FRANCISCO — The California Federation of Labor Unions today gave its sole
endorsement to Supervisor Connie Chan in the race for Congress in CA-11, marking her as the
choice of working people in California. Momentum continues to build for Chan as she racks up
endorsements from top elected officials, community groups and, now, California’s largest labor
organization.

"The heart of our democracy is not found in corporate boardrooms but on the picket lines with
working people. I am deeply honored to earn the sole endorsement of the California Federation
of Labor Unions representing more than 1,300 unions and over two million union members
across our state,” said Connie Chan. “The labor movement has always been the driving force
behind better wages, safer workplaces, and a stronger middle class. I’m proud to stand with the
working people of organized labor, and I will take that fight with me to Congress to protect
workers’ rights and build an economy that works for everyone.”

“Working families need Democrats in Congress who have the backbone to fight for them and
who are unapologetically pro-union. Connie Chan is exactly that kind of leader. California’s labor
movement is proud to give her our sole endorsement because we know she’ll stand up for
workers and fight for good union jobs,” said Lorena Gonzalez, President, California
Federation of Labor Unions.

“In our current economy, working people need leaders who they can count on to side with them
100% – leaders who have walked the picket line and who understand how high the stakes are
at the bargaining table,” said Lizzy Tapia, president of Unite Here Local 2 in San Francisco.
“Connie Chan has shown time and again that she stands with union members and respects the
dignity of working people. Hospitality workers and the entire labor movement are proud to
support her for Congress.”

“Connie Chan understands that strong communities are built by working people and powered by
good union jobs,” said John Doherty, IBEW Local 6 business manager and vice-president of
the San Francisco Building and Construction Trades Council. “She has stood with labor in San
Francisco and proven herself to be an honest leader whose word is her bond and who always
 looks out for working families. As we prepare to replace a legendary leader like Nancy Pelosi,
sending a warrior for the working class like Connie Chan to Congress just makes sense.”

The California Federation of Labor is the statewide affiliate of the AFL-CIO, representing more
than 2.3 million union members and 1,300 unions. It made its official endorsements in
Congressional races at its convention today in Sacramento. This endorsement confirms Chan
as the overwhelming choice of labor and working people. Chan has already earned the support
of the National Education Association, National Nurses United, California Teachers Association,
California Federation of Teachers, San Francisco Labor Council, San Francisco Building and
Construction Trades Council, United Educators of San Francisco, San Francisco Fire Fighters
Local 798, UNITE HERE! Local 2, International Federation of Professional and Technical
Engineers Local 21, International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers Local 6, American
Federation of Teachers 2121, Plumbers, Steamfitters and HVACR Local 38 and Teamsters Joint
Council 7.

A full list of endorsements can be found at ConnieChanSF.com

Connie is running to succeed Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi who announced her retirement late
last year. She has been elected twice to the San Francisco Board of Supervisors in 2020 and
2024, and its Budget Chair since 2023. If elected, Connie would be the first Asian American to
represent San Francisco in Congress.

                                              ###

January 28, 2026
Press@conniechansf.com

     SAN FRANCISCO LABOR COUNCIL ENDORSES CONNIE CHAN FOR CONGRESS

San Francisco - Connie Chan has been endorsed by the San Francisco Labor Council (SFLC)
for her campaign to succeed Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi in California Congressional District
11. SFLC is the local body of the AFL-CIO. Over 150 unions are affiliated with the SFLC,
representing more than 100,000 union members and their families.

“The Labor movement is the answer to rebuilding the middle class because it empowers
everyday people to organize and advocate for a better future collectively. And in solidarity, I am
always proud to stand with workers to fight for better wages, fair contracts, improved benefits
and safe working conditions,” said Connie Chan. “I’m honored to have the support and
endorsement of the working people of San Francisco and I’m ready to fight to bring down the
cost of living so every family can thrive.”

“Workers know we can count on Connie Chan. She doesn’t just drop in at election time - she’s
there with us day in and day out doing the hard work that doesn’t always get headlines but does
get results,” said Mike Casey, President, San Francisco Labor Council. “Speaker Emerita Nancy
Pelosi was our champion in Congress and we need Connie Chan to carry on the fight and be
our voice in Washington, DC.”

On Monday, the Chan campaign announced the support of the two largest unions representing
California teachers, the California Teachers Association and the California Federation of
Teachers joining UNITED HERE Local 2. You can see a full list of endorsements at
Conniechansf.com. With this vote, SFLC made clear there is one candidate for Congress
working people can count on: Connie Chan.
